html:
The Hupacasath are a Nuu-chah-nulth people of the Alberni Valley on Vancouver Island, British Columbia, around today's Port Alberni. The First Nation has about 300 members and claims a large territory of forest and rivers.

Like other Nuu-chah-nulth they lived from salmon, cedar and the sea, and held potlatches. In recent years the small nation drew attention by going to court in 2012 to challenge an investment treaty between Canada and China, arguing it had not been consulted. It lost, but the case made its name known across Canada. Their neighbours to the north are the Kwakwaka'wakw.
